literature_notes: Two ledger lines were examined. L1 (PMC4733052) reports a FLAG-tagged full-length murine HEG1 lentiviral construct expressed in endothelial cells, but neither the quote nor the surrounding text names a terminus or residue for the FLAG insertion. HEG1 is a type I single-pass transmembrane protein with one extracellular N-terminus (after SP cleavage at residue 29/30) and one intracellular C-terminus (residues 1271–1381); FLAG tags are used at both termini in the literature, so the topology alone cannot resolve which face carries the tag without knowing it is extracellular. The topology-derived rule requires that the tag be known to be on the surface before the single extracellular terminus can be inferred as the position; that prerequisite is not met here. The site was therefore dropped. L2 (PMC11001532) reports a pCMV6-HEG1-MycDDK (Origene RC212168) construct with an explicitly C-terminal Myc-DDK tag transfected into HAECs. The C-terminus of HEG1 is intracellular (residues 1271–1381), so this tag faces the cytoplasm and does not qualify as an extracellular surface site; it is recorded in other_positions.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal Myc-DDK tag (Origene pCMV6-HEG1-MycDDK RC212168) appended after the last residue F1381, which lies in the intracellular tail (residues 1271–1381); not a surface tag.
